title: Twins activate Ryan Jeffers from 10-day IL, will carry three catchers for now
content:
The Minnesota Twins activated catcher Ryan Jeffers from the 10-day IL on Friday, giving them their starting catcher and one of their most consistent hitters back in the lineup for the final series before the All-Star break.

Jeffers was in the midst of an All-Star-caliber season — hitting .295 with seven homers and a .949 OPS through 37 games — when he broke his left hamate bone on May 18.

“I feel good,” Jeffers said to Minnesota-based reporters, including The Athletic’s Dan Hayes, on Thursday. “I felt pretty good this weekend but wanted to go down to Iowa (for a minor league road trip) and get some more games, get a larger sample size. I felt like I was tracking the ball well, getting back in the groove of things.”

Jeffers played in five rehab games with Triple-A St. Paul and hit .375/.474/.813 in 19 plate appearances. Outfielder Kyler Fedko was optioned to St. Paul as the corresponding move. The Twins will carry three catchers — Jeffers, Victor Caratini and Alex Jackson — for now.

There was legitimate concern about how Jeffers’ absence would impact the Twins’ offense, but they have stayed surprisingly competitive since. Though they are 46-48, the Twins are just two games back in the American League Central and one game out of the final AL wild-card spot.  They also lead the AL in runs scored (459).

Part of that is because of the production they’ve seen from  Caratini and Jackson. Caratini was the Twins’ best hitter by OPS in June with a whopping 1.059, and Jackson has been more than serviceable (.296/.321/.407 overall) in the backup role.

That makes the timing of Jeffers’ return all the more intriguing. The Twins have yet to decide on a direction for this year’s trade deadline, but Jeffers, 29, could be a top trade candidate. He’ll be a free agent at the end of the year. Both the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays have needs at catcher.

The Twins will face the Los Angeles Angels before the All-Star break begins. Right-hander Zebby Matthews is tabbed for Friday’s start against Grayson Rodriguez.
